Search conducted by Agent Hoehle and the undersigned at

evidence. Thereupon the investigating officers proceeded
to the garage of the house, which as it appeared was turned
for a use as a room and was occupied by one Mogilkin.
The tenant Mogilkine flatly refused to admit the officers
into his room stating that officers had no authority to
search private dwelling places. As the undersigned was
not able to persuade Mogilkine that the search was to
be conducted in accordance with instructions received and
it was apparent that he was ready to resort to violence
to prevent the officers to execute their duty.

In view of the above situation Agent Hoehle and the undersigned
proceeded to obtain assistance from Lokawei Station and instructions
as to the further action. The undersigned reported the situation
to Mr. Liao and was instructed to get uniform policemen from
Lokawei Station and to proceed with the search.

Accordingly, the officers in question accompanied by two
C.P.U.S proceeded to the above mentioned address and entered
the room in question. The occupant of the room Mogilkine became
very abusive and violent and the C.P.U.S had to restrain him.
He was cautioned by the undersigned that it is a criminal offence
according to the law of this country to obstruct officers in
execution of duty. The search was carried out but only
small items were found which Agent Hoehle did not want to
have confiscated.

外事科 ____________________ 1946年5月4日。

协助美国陆军刑事调查处办公室。

今日上午10时20分，美国陆军刑事调查处办公室的霍勒（Hoehle）探员来到本办公室，请求协助搜查林尼亚台（Linia Terrace）20号由E.M. 季霍诺夫（Tichonov）占用的房间以及该房屋的 garage（车库）。根据夏先生收到的指示，本人前往上述地址。

霍勒探员和本人在E.M. 季霍诺夫占用的房间进行的搜查未发现任何证据。随后，调查人员前往该房屋的车库，该车库似乎已被改作房间使用，并由一名莫吉尔金（Mogilkin）占用。租户莫吉尔金断然拒绝让官员进入他的房间，声称官员无权搜查私人住所。由于本人无法说服莫吉尔金相信搜查是根据收到的指示进行的，而且显然他准备诉诸暴力以阻止官员执行职务。

鉴于上述情况，霍勒探员和本人前往老闸捕房寻求协助及进一步行动的指示。本人向廖先生报告了情况，并奉命从老闸捕房调派制服警察，继续进行搜查。

因此，有关官员在两名中国籍美国警务人员（C.P.U.S.）的陪同下前往上述地址并进入了涉事房间。房间 occupant（居住者）莫吉尔金变得非常辱骂性和暴力，中国籍美国警务人员不得不将其制服。本人警告他，根据本国法律，阻碍官员执行职务属于刑事犯罪。搜查进行了，但只发现了一些小件物品，霍勒探员不希望予以没收。

在整个过程中，莫吉尔金继续大声叫骂各种污言秽语，主要针对中国警察部队和美国军队。他说道：“中国警察是一伙强盗，与美国军官分赃”，“苏联政府将教导美国人和中国人如何抢劫苏联公民”，“我已经在苏联报纸上写过关于美军匪徒般行径的文章，我还要再写”。他对本人说，你是

a t aiter to your country - you emmigrants worked with
the Japanese and now you collaborate with Chinese and
Americans", "I will kill you when I meet you on the

The undersigned does wish to record here all the obscene
and vile expressions which were uttered by Mogilkins both
in Russian and English language. The C.I.D. agent and two

I may mention that it was entirely due to the patience of

I have every reason to believe that it was the intention of
Mogilkine to create an incident by his provocative
attitude to the C.I.D. and Police to serve the aim of
propaganda.

SUBJECT:- Communication dated 23-10-46 from Security

The correct name of the person who forms the subject of
the attached communication is,probably, Liubov Mihailovna SOU-
VOROVA ; Russian,born 18-1-1920 at Vladivostok,Russia. Accord-
ing to her own statement, she arrived in Shanghai from Vladivo-
stok via Genzan (Korea) in 1922 together with her parents. Un-
til 25-3-43 she was registered with the Russian Emigrants Com-
mittee,118/1 Moulmein Road,but afterwards became a Soviet citi-
zen. When registering with the Police in November,1942 she
gave her address as 129 Route Vallon,Apt 3 and her occupation
- as that of a hat-maker, and described herself as a spinster.
No report has since been made to the Police as to her marriage,
and therefore there is no record of her under the name/of PARKER or
TUCKER.

at Vladivostok,who on 6-2-36 was arraigned before the Chinese
Court by the former French Police for " Abandon du domicile ma-
ternel " ( abandoning mother's home ) and was ordered by the

附件函件中所述之人的正确姓名可能是：柳博芙·米哈伊洛夫娜·苏沃洛娃（Liubov Mihailovna SOUVOROVA）；俄罗斯人，1920年1月18日出生于俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克。据其自称，她于1922年与父母一起从符拉迪沃斯托克经元山（朝鲜）抵达上海。直到1943年3月25日，她在慕尔鸣路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记，但后来成为苏联公民。1942年11月在警察局登记时，她提供的地址是华伦路（Route Vallon）129号3室，职业为制帽匠，并自称未婚。此后未向警方报告其婚姻状况，因此没有以帕克（PARKER）或塔克（TUCKER）为名的记录。

她可能与一名“卢巴·苏沃洛娃”（Luba SOUVOROVA）为同一人，该人1920年1月18日出生于符拉迪沃斯托克，曾于1936年2月6日因“遗弃母家”（Abandon du domicile maternel）被前法租界巡捕房起诉至中国法院，并被法院命令交由慈善团体监护。除此之外，本科对该人没有任何不利的了解。

December, 19th, 1945.

STATEMENT.

The following is the voluntary statement I am making to D.S.I., Brauns
of Shanghai Police.

My name is Mrs Olga P. KUHNE, nee HOFF, age 25, Russian, divorced,
residing at 588, Route de Zikawei.

I became acquainted with Major O'Connell in the end of October, 1945.
Although I do not remember the exact circumstances under which I became
acquainted with him, but I believe that he was brought to my home as a
guest by some mutual friend. We became very friendly and he occasionally
stayed at my home overnight. He moved into my place a few days ago, when
he found out that he was to leave shortly for the U.S. He brought with
him only few belongings, which he did not intend to take with him to
U.S. He mentioned to me that he intended to return to Shanghai on
January 5th, 1946.

Apart from his personal belongings (clothing and blankets) he brought
on two occasions a quantity of U.S. Army canned assorted foodstuffs.
We used these goods together. The remaining 45 tins of assorted food
and juices were seized this day by U.S. Army C.I.D. assisted by
Shanghai Police. I do not believe that Major O'Connell ever sold any
of such foodstuffs, because I heard him telling Mrs GLEINIKOFF,
that such goods were not for sale.

Two bottles of vitamins (U.S. Army property) were used by Major O'Connell
personally. One of them is still full and the other partly consumed.

Regarding the box of whisky found by the Army C.I.D. and Shanghai Police
at my place, I remember it as property of Mr Boris GLEINIKOFF. When I
saw the whisky I asked Major O'Connell, if it were his property. Major
answered in negative stating that it was the property of "Boris" (Gleinikoff).

I believe that Major O'Connell and Boris GLEINIKOFF have regular business
relations, as I understand that Mr GLEINIKOFF sells various goods to
U.S. Armed Forces. I never heard of Mr GLEINIKOFF buying anything from
Major O'Connell. I believe that Major Mr GLEINIKOFF deals in all sort of
foodstuffs and liquors including whisky.

The above is my complete and true statement.

Mrs. O. F. Kuhne†
Olga P. KUHNE

供词。

以下是我向上海警察局特别调查员 Brauns 作出的自愿供词。

我叫 Olga P. KUHNE 女士，娘家姓 HOFF，25岁，俄国人，离异，居住在西爱威路（Route de Zikawei）588号。

我于1945年10月底结识了 O'Connell 少校。虽然我不记得与他相识的确切情形，但我相信他是通过一位共同的朋友作为客人被带到我家的。我们变得非常友好，他偶尔会在我家过夜。几天前，当他得知自己即将离开前往美国时，便搬到了我那里。他只带来了几件他不打算带去美国的随身物品。他向我提到，他打算于1946年1月5日返回上海。

除了他的个人物品（衣物和毯子）外，他还分两次带来了一定数量的美军杂项罐头食品。我们一起食用了这些物品。剩余的45罐杂项食品和果汁于今日由美国陆军刑事调查处在上海警方的协助下查获。我不相信 O'Connell 少校曾出售过任何此类食品，因为我听他对 GLEINIKOFF 女士说，这些物品是非卖品。

两瓶维生素（美军财产）由 O'Connell 少校个人使用。其中一瓶仍是满的，另一瓶已部分消耗。

关于军队刑事调查处和上海警方在我处发现的那箱威士忌，我记得那是 Boris GLEINIKOFF 先生的财产。当我看到威士忌时，我问 O'Connell 少校那是否是他的财产。少校予以否认，并称那是“Boris”（Gleinikoff）的财产。

我相信 O'Connell 少校和 Boris GLEINIKOFF 之间有定期的业务关系，据我了解，GLEINIKOFF 先生向美军出售各种商品。我从未听说 GLEINIKOFF 先生从 O'Connell 少校那里购买任何东西。我相信 GLEINIKOFF 先生经营各类食品和酒类，包括威士忌。

以上是我完整且真实的供词。

O. F. Kuhne† 夫人
Olga P. KUHNE

STATEMENT.

I, the undersigned, Boris M. OLMENIKOFF, Russian, age 25, married,
residing at 62, Route de Secours, beg to submit the following
voluntary statement:

Following the capitulation of Japan I became a feedstuffs contractor to
Emergency Team for the care for civil internees in Shanghai area. Due to
subsequent changes inorganisation of the above body, I became a contractor
for the American Army in Navy dealing in the same kind of goods.

I made through my business relations many acquaintances and among them with
Major O'Connell. We became good friends and he used to visit me at my home
and we used to go together to various places of entertainment.

On about December 20th, 1945 an auction of old canteen stocks of now dissolved
Russian Auxiliary Detachment of Shanghai Police was to take place. I
visited the canteen premises and saw there among some other goods a
quantity of whiskey. I mentioned the same fact to Major O'Connell, Colonel
Kearney and some other officers, whilst we were attending together a
party held at some private house. I expressed my opinion that whiskey could
be purchased at a cheaper price at this particular auction than anywhere
else in Shanghai. Major O'Connell and me approached the auctioneers
(L. Moore & Co, Ltd) a day or two before the auction. As I understand
that American officers are not permitted to engage themselves in business
transactions and conducted negotiations myself, stating in presence of
Major O'Connell, that I was acting on behalf of certain American officers
and requested them to sell some boxes of whiskey privately and before
the auction to us, giving as the reason that the buyers were the officers
of American Army i.e. the allied nation of auctioneers (a British concern).

However the auctioneers declined the request stating that such
preferential treatment would be irregular and that the goods in questioned
were to be sold at the public auction.

As Major O'Connell and the other officers were short of money at that time
I came to auction with my own money. As Major O'Connell could not be located
before the auction I went to the auction accompanied by Colonel Kearney.
Colonel Kearney stipulated that the highest price they were prepared to pay
was to be U.S.$4.20 per bottle. However, as the auction was well attended
and bidding went very lively the price soon exceeded the above mentioned
ceiling price. I consulted with Colonel Kearney and the latter cautioned

供词。

本人，下述签署人 Boris M. OLMENIKOFF，俄国人，25岁，已婚，居住在救济路（Route de Secours）62号，谨提交以下自愿供词：

日本投降后，我成为负责照顾上海地区平民被拘禁者的紧急小组的食品承包商。由于上述机构随后的组织变更，我成为海军美军的承包商，经营同类商品。

我通过业务关系结识了许多人，其中包括 O'Connell 少校。我们成了好朋友，他常来我家拜访，我们也常一起去各种娱乐场所。

大约在1945年12月20日，现已解散的上海公共租界工部局警务处俄国辅助分队（Russian Auxiliary Detachment）的旧食堂库存将进行拍卖。我参观了食堂场所，在那里除其他一些物品外，看到了一定数量的威士忌。当我们在某私人住宅参加聚会时，我向 O'Connell 少校、Kearney 上校和其他一些军官提到了这一事实。我表示我的看法是，在这次特定的拍卖会上购买威士忌的价格比在上海任何其他地方都便宜。在拍卖会前一两天，我和 O'Connell 少校接触了拍卖师（L. Moore & Co, Ltd）。据我了解，美国军官不允许参与商业交易，因此我自己进行了谈判，并在 O'Connell 少校面前声明，我是代表某些美国军官行事，并要求他们在拍卖前私下将几箱威士忌卖给我们，理由是买家是美国陆军军官，即拍卖商（一家英国公司）的盟国人员。

然而，拍卖商拒绝了这一请求，称这种优待是不规范的，且 questioned 货物必须在公开拍卖中出售。

由于 O'Connell 少校和其他军官当时资金短缺，我用自己的钱参加了拍卖。由于在拍卖前找不到 O'Connell 少校，我在 Kearney 上校的陪同下参加了拍卖。Kearney 上校规定他们愿意支付的最高价格为每瓶4.20美元。然而，由于拍卖会出席人数众多，竞价非常激烈，价格很快超过了上述上限价格。我与 Kearney 上校商议，后者警告说

so that his and his friends participation in business is limited by the
fact that they were prepared to buy the goods in question at marketable
prices. Should I continue to bid I was to take the risk myself.

Finally I purchase 14 boxes of whiskey and 1 box of brandy at the price of
about U.S.$6.20 per bottle. When the purchased goods were delivered I
stored the same at my home, delivering after a day or two 3 boxes to
Major O'Connel's quarters Room 525, Cathay Mansions, Rue Cardinal Mercier.

As far as the payment for the purchased goods is concerned the situation was
as follows. When the auction in question was over I made a partpayment to
the auctioneers, paying CNC$800,000.00 the balance of CNC$600,000 remained
outstanding. On the following day I went to Major O'Connel requesting him
to pay some money to meet the outstanding account. Major O'Connel stated
that at the time he had no money on hands, but promised to get the necessary
amount in a short while. In about 4 days after the auction he gave me
US$500.00. As this amount still represented less than required CNC$600,000.00
I had to pay another CNC$200,000.00 of my own money, so as to have the
purchased property delivered by auctioneers. I understand that US$500.00
given to me by Major O'Connel were either received him as a repayment of
a previously loaned money, or as a loan.

The above is the only private business transaction which I made with Major
O'Connel, with whose office I deal as a contractor selling foodstuffs.

Regarding the whiskey case I must state that we never entered in any detailed
or even general agreement as to disposal of profits or shares to be contributed
by parties concerned. The deal was of rather friendly than purely business
nature.

The above is the complete and true statement of the facts as they came
to my knowledge.

Boris Oleinnikoff

他和他的朋友参与商业活动受到限制，因为他们只准备以市场价格购买相关货物。如果我继续竞价，风险需由我自己承担。

最后，我以每瓶约6.20美元的价格购买了14箱威士忌和1箱白兰地。当购买的货物交付时，我将它们存放在我家，一两天后将3箱送到了 O'Connel 少校的住处，位于梅神父路（Rue Cardinal Mercier）国泰公寓（Cathay Mansions）525室。

关于所购货物的付款情况如下。当上述拍卖结束后，我向拍卖商支付了部分款项，支付了法币800,000.00元，剩余法币600,000.00元未付。第二天，我去找 O'Connel 少校，请求他支付一些钱以结清未付账款。O'Connel 少校表示当时手头没钱，但承诺不久后会凑齐所需金额。拍卖后大约4天，他给了我500.00美元。由于这笔金额仍少于所需的法币600,000.00元，我不得不再自掏腰包支付法币200,000.00元，以便让拍卖商交付所购财产。我理解 O'Connel 少校给我的500.00美元，要么是他偿还之前借出的款项，要么是作为贷款。

这是我与 O'Connel 少校进行的唯一私人商业交易，我作为承包商向其办公室出售食品。

关于威士忌一案，我必须声明，我们就利润处置或各方应承担的股份从未达成任何详细甚至一般的协议。这笔交易更多是出于友情而非纯粹的商业性质。

以上是我所知事实的完整且真实的陈述。

Boris Oleinnikoff
